AxiomAcceptance: AcceptedVersion: 1.0.0-candidate.1

A foundational proposition about the world or domain that the model takes as given and builds around. It is not a requirement on the system’s behavior; revising it requires reviewing what depends on it.

When it applies
Use "axiom" for the load-bearing truths a project stands on and reasons *from* — the ones that justify why a whole area, method, or rule family exists. Three tests: (1) can the system make it false? If yes, it is an invariant, not an axiom. (2) Is it actually believed true, or is it a bet? A bet (`veracidade: low`) is a **premise**, not an axiom. (3) Does a family derive from it? If nothing does, it is inert.
Record formats
No record-type contract in this selected catalog declares this exact definition among the meanings it uses.
A stated exclusion
Admission, activation, publication, release, deployment, and external effects.
Formal definition, source explanation and boundaries

The formal statement governs the meaning. The short introduction above helps you read it; it does not replace its requirements.

Source explanatory wording

A truth you build on, not a rule you obey. "Creatives are fat-tailed" is true about the world; you design around it. If it turned out false, your plan was wrong — not your code.

Exact governing statement

Axiom is the normalized definition identified by semantic.axiom, owned within scope.shared-authority, and carried by type.definition. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D53 without silently merging it with another target.

Bound source-semantic basis:

An axiom is a **foundational proposition taken as given** — bedrock the system does not derive further within itself and holds as true (high commitment/veracity) — **from which a family of premises, invariants, and constitution rules derives**, such that revising it forces rethinking everything built on it. Its defining subject is the **world or domain** the system operates in: an axiom states *why* the system is shaped as it is, and the system is **built around** it rather than made to satisfy it. It is **not** a constraint on the system's own behavior — that is an invariant (`CAV2-D54`).

```text
axiom A:  taken-as-given(A) ∧ ¬derives-within-system(A) ∧ veracity(A) = high
          ∧ fan_out(A) = { premises, invariants, constitution-rules derived from A }
subject(A) = world/domain          (not the system's own behavior)
system can violate A?  No — if A is false, the premise was wrong, not the code buggy
genesis:       invariant → "why must this hold?" → A     (discovery order)
justification: A → invariant → constitution rule          (top-down order)
```

The **fan-out** is the axiom's signature: a proposition that grounds only one
downstream item, and nothing else, is not an axiom but the restatement of a single
invariant.
  • An axiom is **not** an invariant (`CAV2-D54`): the invariant is a must-hold on the *system*; the axiom is a given truth about the *world* the system is built around. It is **not** a premise: a premise is a working bet held at low veracity (`veracidade: low`), an axiom is held true. It is **not** a constitution (`CAV2-D58`): the constitution is the authoritative scoped rulebook; the axiom is the reason behind it. It is **not** a definition (`CAV2-D33`): a definition assigns meaning to a term, an axiom asserts a foundational truth. An axiom and the invariants it grounds enforce nothing by themselves. A constitution authorizes and scopes constraints; a selected validator or gate checks or performs enforcement.

Bounded Self-Application InvariantAcceptance: AcceptedVersion: 1.0.0-candidate.1

A governed process may be applied to its own outputs only when every recursive step identifies its scope, owner, review gate, carried state or residue, how results will be recombined, and a stopping condition.

When it applies
Use bounded recursive self-application when definitions-governance defines definition work, Craft records and routes work about Craft, CyberAlchemy applies its method to CyberAlchemy method artifacts, or a tower creates a higher-layer artifact that must explain back down to its source.
Record formats
No record-type contract in this selected catalog declares this exact definition among the meanings it uses.
A stated exclusion
Admission, activation, publication, release, deployment, and external effects.
Formal definition, source explanation and boundaries

The formal statement governs the meaning. The short introduction above helps you read it; it does not replace its requirements.

Source explanatory wording

The system can use its own method on its own work, but each loop needs a label, a boundary, a reviewer, and a way back.

Exact governing statement

Bounded Self-Application Invariant is the normalized invariant identified by semantic.bounded-self-application-invariant, owned within scope.shared-authority, and carried by type.invariant. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D30 without silently merging it with another target.

Bound source-semantic basis:

Bounded recursive self-application is the CyberAlchemy v2 invariant that a governed process may be applied to artifacts produced by that same process only when each recursive step declares its artifact, altitude or layer, scope, owner, gate, carried state or residue, recomposition path, and stopping condition.

The recursive move must preserve authority boundaries: the process, the artifact being processed, the owner route, and the resulting authority posture must remain distinct unless an explicit promotion or coupling records otherwise.

Given a governed process `P`, an artifact `a_n` already produced, shaped, or
maintained by `P`, and an altitude marker `h_n`, a valid recursive
self-application step has the form:

```text
P_hn(a_n) -> a_(n+1) at h_(n+1)
```

The step is admissible only if it records:

- source artifact `a_n`
- target artifact `a_(n+1)`
- altitude or layer relation between `h_n` and `h_(n+1)`
- owner route
- gate or validation condition
- residue or state carried forward
- recomposition path back to the lower artifact or parent context
- stopping condition, budget, or explicit next owner

Without those fields, the move is ordinary recursion, self-hosting, looped work,
or open residue, not CyberAlchemy v2 recursivity.
  • Bounded recursive self-application is not ordinary code recursion, not generic self-hosting, not endless reflection, not child-folder nesting, not automatic promotion, and not a license to run agents recursively without a budget. It does not replace `CAV2-D17` reflection tower method or `CAV2-D20` Craft method; it governs when process-on-own-artifact moves are admissible across those and other methods.

Canonical Package HomeAcceptance: AcceptedVersion: 1.0.0-candidate.1

The designated package containing material that changes together. Distinct capabilities, contexts, products and runtime records remain separately identified within it; other catalogs point to it rather than keeping competing master copies.

When it applies
Selecting the single governed artifact tree that carries the canonical machine sources of one explicitly declared owner-local aggregate and keeps its related semantic facets cohesive without collapsing their identities.
Record formats
Canonical package manifest · v1
A stated exclusion
Inferring semantic identity, context membership, or authority from a directory path.
Formal definition, source explanation and boundaries

The formal statement governs the meaning. The short introduction above helps you read it; it does not replace its requirements.

Source explanatory wording

Keep one thing that changes together in one canonical workshop. The workshop can contain separately labelled capability, context, product, runtime, and evidence benches; putting them together does not make them the same thing. Catalogs elsewhere point to the workshop instead of keeping rival master copies.

Exact governing statement

A Canonical Package Home is the unique governed artifact tree H selected for an owner-local aggregate A by an explicit lifecycle-owner binding and unit-of-change declaration. H carries A's canonical machine sources. Capability, bounded-context, product, DomainSpec, implementation, evidence, and projection facets may be colocated in H when they share A's lifecycle, but their identities and authorities remain distinct and are connected by explicit typed relations. Indexes and global views may reference or generate projections of H; they must not duplicate its canonical carriers.

CPH(A)=H iff declared_owner(A)=lifecycle_owner(H) and unit_of_change(A)=unit_of_change(H); exists exactly one H for each canonical carrier c in A such that canonical_at(c,H); colocated(x,y,H) =/=> identity(x)=identity(y); classified_as(x,k) =/=> CPH(x)=root(k); indexes(i,c) =/=> canonical_at(c,i).
  • The lifecycle owner and unit of change select the home; the directory does not select the owner, identity, or context.
  • Semantic orthogonality requires distinct identities and typed relations, not separate physical roots.
  • A bounded context may be a facet of an aggregate without being the aggregate's directory or owning every colocated artifact.
  • Artifacts with different lifecycle owners or independent recovery boundaries require separate canonical homes even when one global index presents them together.

Canonical Representation InvariantAcceptance: AcceptedVersion: 1.0.0-candidate.1

Requires one designated machine representation for each artifact and an owner-approved process-origin declaration for its kind. Generated human views do not gain independent authority, and origin assurance does not establish truth.

When it applies
Use when deciding whether a document is a first-class typed artifact or an ungoverned working note. Ask: does it instantiate an enumerated canonical kind, does its owner admit one exact allowed origin, and does the record state how strongly that origin statement is supported? Under the current review-mode posture, `declared` is sufficient for owner admission, but the artifact must be described as owner-declared rather than mechanically verified process output.
Record formats
No record-type contract in this selected catalog declares this exact definition among the meanings it uses.
A stated exclusion
Admission, activation, publication, release, deployment, and external effects.
Formal definition, source explanation and boundaries

The formal statement governs the meaning. The short introduction above helps you read it; it does not replace its requirements.

Source explanatory wording

Store one machine truth, generate the readable view from it, and never let the folder name or generated text become a second authority.

Exact governing statement

Canonical Representation Invariant is the normalized invariant identified by semantic.canonical-representation-invariant, owned within scope.shared-authority, and carried by type.invariant. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D51 without silently merging it with another target.

Target-specific normative meaning:

Canonical Representation Invariant requires each artifact to have exactly one declared machine-canonical representation; human views and convenience labels are generated projections, directory placement cannot establish type or authority, and every admitted canonical kind must bind an owner-approved process origin with an honest assurance level.

Bound source-semantic basis:

A canonical artifact is an artifact instance whose **kind is a member of the canonical-kind enumeration** (Canonical kinds) and whose responsible owner has admitted an exact `process_origin` declaration that names one allowed producer and process for that kind. It therefore carries a defined type (a `CAV2-D21` classification/schema facet that is bound, not left as residue) and an owner-declared process origin.

The strength of support for the origin declaration is recorded separately as `origin_assurance`:

- `declared` means an owner or source made the exact origin statement; - `integrity-bound` means a verifier confirmed that the statement and bound artifact-state bytes match an L1 integrity mechanism; and - `actor-attested` means an identified actor attested the exact tuple under a bound L2 identity policy and external signature.

`actor-attested` is a defined future level, not a currently available result. No assurance level proves that the named process actually executed, that the statement is true, or that the artifact is correct or authoritative.

Canonical-ness is therefore the property of *being typed and carrying an owner-admitted, allowed process-origin declaration with an honest assurance level*. It is **decoupled from authority** — a canonical artifact may be non-authoritative and still canonical. An artifact whose kind is not in the enumeration, or whose exact origin does not resolve to an owner-approved producer for that kind, is non-canonical or remains blocked as typed residue.

```text
OriginAssurance = { declared, integrity-bound, actor-attested }

allowed_origin(a)
  <-> (producer_ref(a), process_ref(a), process_version_ref(a))
      in allowed_origins(canonical_kind(a))

canonical(a)
  <-> canonical_kind(a) in CanonicalKinds
      and owner_admitted(a)
      and allowed_origin(a)
      and origin_assurance(a) in OriginAssurance

CanonicalKinds  superset-of  AuthorityKinds   (every authority-kind is a canonical-kind;
                                               not every canonical-kind bears authority)
canonical(a)   independent-of   authoritative(a)   (authority is earned via CAV2-D48)
```

Each canonical artifact declares exactly one `canonical_kind` and one exact
`process_origin` record, and inherits from its kind the `authority_kind` it rolls
up to and its `CAV2-D52` durability. The inherited fields are derived, not
asserted: an artifact cannot choose its `authority_kind`.

`allowed_origins(kind)` is intentionally set-valued because one kind may have
more than one allowed producer. The artifact still binds one exact producer,
process, version, and origin statement. The allowed set must come from a current
owner-approved source; the candidate canonical-kind table does not become
authority through this definition. An unresolved or candidate-only producer
cannot establish canonical origin.
  • Canonical artifact is **not** authority and **not** "canonical source": the store's existing *canonical source*, *canonical section*, and *canonical definition* (alias of `CAV2-D33`) use *canonical = the authoritative version*; this term uses *canonical = has a canonical form + owner-admitted process-origin declaration* and is explicitly decoupled from authority. The legacy alias `process-born` must not be used to imply observed execution unless a separately governed execution witness supports that claim. It is **not** the enumeration itself — that is the set of kinds in `CANONICAL-KINDS.md`; a canonical artifact is a member instance. It does not promote anything: earning authority is `CAV2-D48`, being a recognized kind is `CAV2-D49`. Origin assurance is not proof, trust, validation, truth, discharge, promotion, adoption, or publication. Prior 2026-06-21 review prose that used "canonical artifact" to mean "target-owned / deployed authority" is the *authoritative-version* sense and predates this term (recorded in [DEFINITION-DRIFT-AUDIT.md](DEFINITION-DRIFT-AUDIT.md)).
  • This target remains distinct from the sibling targets semantic.artifact reconstructed from CAV2-D51; shared source lineage does not merge their identities or validation purposes.

Claim-Support Compatibility InvariantAcceptance: AcceptedVersion: 1.0.0-candidate.1

A claim’s strength, status or authority effect must stay within the proof, evidence, owner decision or accepted premise offered to support it. Partial or missing support must remain explicit.

When it applies
Use claim <= proof when writing research findings, definitions, constitutions, validation reports, ontology projections, public statements, or implementation readiness notes. The invariant forces the project to ask: what exactly supports this claim, and how strong may the wording be?
Record formats
No record-type contract in this selected catalog declares this exact definition among the meanings it uses.
A stated exclusion
Admission, activation, publication, release, deployment, and external effects.
Formal definition, source explanation and boundaries

The formal statement governs the meaning. The short introduction above helps you read it; it does not replace its requirements.

Source explanatory wording

Do not say more than the evidence can carry.

Exact governing statement

Claim-Support Compatibility Invariant is the normalized invariant identified by semantic.claim-support-compatibility-invariant, owned within scope.shared-authority, and carried by type.invariant. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D38 without silently merging it with another target.

Bound source-semantic basis:

Claim <= proof is the CyberAlchemy v2 epistemic invariant that a claim's asserted strength, authority effect, validation status, or publication posture must not exceed the proof, evidence, witness, validation result, owner decision, or accepted premise cited for it.

If support is absent, partial, private, indirect, disputed, or weaker than the claim, the claim must be downgraded, marked as hypothesis or candidate, flagged with residue, routed through a gate, or blocked from governing work.

For claim `c`, asserted strength `S(c)`, and support package `P(c)`:

```text
S(c) <= strength(P(c))
```

where `strength(P(c))` is interpreted by the relevant domain, validator,
research standard, owner decision, or constitution. If no support package is
declared, `S(c)` defaults to candidate or hypothesis.
  • Proof does not mean only formal mathematical proof. It can be a source citation, validation run, witness, owner decision, accepted premise, or formal proof, depending on the claim type. The invariant does not require maximal certainty; it requires honest wording relative to declared support.

Classification AxisAcceptance: AcceptedVersion: 1.0.0-candidate.1

One declared question used to classify something, such as its kind or lifecycle state. Its answers have a distinct decision or checking purpose.

When it applies
Use orthogonal classification when adding taxonomy, ontology, status, confidence, maturity, source-role, node-type, or task-kind labels. The action must answer what new distinction the classification adds, what existing axes it could be confused with, and whether any unavoidable dependency is explicitly typed.
Record formats
No record-type contract in this selected catalog declares this exact definition among the meanings it uses.
A stated exclusion
Admission, activation, publication, release, deployment, and external effects.
Formal definition, source explanation and boundaries

The formal statement governs the meaning. The short introduction above helps you read it; it does not replace its requirements.

Source explanatory wording

It is one question in a classification, such as what something means or what lifecycle state it has.

Exact governing statement

Classification Axis is the normalized definition identified by semantic.classification-axis, owned within scope.shared-authority, and carried by type.definition. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D22 without silently merging it with another target.

Target-specific normative meaning:

A Classification Axis is one explicitly named, independently valued dimension used to classify an artifact or concept for a distinct decision or validation purpose.

Bound source-semantic basis:

Orthogonal classification is the CyberAlchemy v2 rule that a governed classification axis, taxonomy label, or ontology grouping is admissible only when it contributes a distinction that is not silently redundant with an existing axis, label, owner lane, lifecycle state, schema field, or typed relation.

A classification is orthogonal when changing it does not secretly change a different authority axis. If a proposed classification cannot stay independent, its dependency must be represented through `CAV2-D16` typed coupling invariant before it can govern downstream work.

For a classified artifact `x`, let:

```text
K(x) = (k_1, k_2, ..., k_n)
```

where each `k_i` is an owned classification axis. A proposed axis `k_p` is
admissible when it contributes a unique operational distinction that cannot be
derived from the existing `K(x)`, or when every dependency between `k_p` and an
existing axis is recorded as a typed coupling with direction, owner, evidence,
and effect.

When data exists, an implementation may use mutual-information, entropy, or
retrieval-precision checks as evidence for uniqueness. When data does not
exist, review must name the unique question, routing decision, or validation
effect the classification adds.

In this definition, orthogonality is an admission and compression discipline:
it asks whether a label or axis contributes independent operational
information. It is not Hilbert-space orthogonality, not a contextuality
obstruction, and not a proof that cross-document consistency has been achieved.
Consistency claims must come from typed relations, schema rules, validators, or
owner decisions, not from the word "orthogonal" by itself.
  • Orthogonal classification is not a requirement that every classifier be statistically proven before exploratory work begins. It is also not isolation: classifications may interact, but the interaction must be represented through a typed coupling, schema rule, or explicit residue. This term does not authorize treating Shannon-style label independence and Hilbert-style projector orthogonality as the same formal object. Any bridge between classification independence and contextuality machinery must be recorded as a separate typed coupling or rejected residue. The imported house_project label system remains source evidence. CyberAlchemy v2 may adopt the orthogonality rule without adopting that source's exact node types, labels, metrics, or status vocabulary.
  • This target remains distinct from the sibling targets semantic.classification-orthogonality-invariant reconstructed from CAV2-D22; shared source lineage does not merge their identities or validation purposes.

Closed Authority-Kind InvariantAcceptance: AcceptedVersion: 1.0.0-candidate.1

Requires authority-bearing kinds to belong to an explicitly closed allowed set, with an owner and declared lifecycle. A new kind is blocked pending an owner decision; the source distinguishes this rule from still-pending deterministic enforcement.

When it applies
Use when a new *type* of authority appears (a new **kind**, not a new artifact of an existing kind). Live open instance: `AUTHORITY-MODEL` OQ-2 — `invariant` and `axiom` govern (`CAV2-D16`/`D29`/`D38`) yet sit outside the kind table.
Record formats
No record-type contract in this selected catalog declares this exact definition among the meanings it uses.
A stated exclusion
Admission, activation, publication, release, deployment, and external effects.
Formal definition, source explanation and boundaries

The formal statement governs the meaning. The short introduction above helps you read it; it does not replace its requirements.

Source explanatory wording

A new *type* of authority can't start governing just because it appeared. Until it is on the official list of kinds — with its lifecycle and owner — anything of that kind is blocked.

Exact governing statement

Closed Authority-Kind Invariant is the normalized invariant identified by semantic.closed-authority-kind-invariant, owned within scope.shared-authority, and carried by type.invariant. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D49 without silently merging it with another target.

Bound source-semantic basis:

Closed authority-kind enumeration is the invariant that the set of authority **kinds** is a closed enumeration (the `Authority model` Authority Kinds table). An artifact whose kind is **not** in that enumeration may not acquire or exercise authority — it defaults to **blocked** pending an owner decision that adds the kind to the enumeration with its declared lifecycle (`CAV2-D48`) and owner route. Adding a kind is itself owner-gated.

```text
CAKE: Kinds is closed; for an artifact of kind k,
  k in Kinds      -> governed by k's own ladder/owner
  k not in Kinds  -> default-deny (blocked) until an owner amends Kinds
```

This **extends** `CAV2-D41` (which assumes a kind/owner exists and says "route to
it") to the case it assumes away — a kind with no enumerated owner/ladder yet.
  • Scoped to authority **kinds** (the enumeration), not individual artifacts (that is the Authority Rule, `CAV2-D41`) and not the per-artifact promotion path (`CAV2-D48` + the promotion-policy ladder). Promoting this definition did not by itself enact the kind table as closed-with-default-deny. Review-mode enactment now lives in the [AUTHORITY-MODEL catch-all row](Authority model#authority-kinds); deterministic enforcement remains pending.

Conformance says that one exact thing meets one exact contract for a clearly named scope, backed by enough current evidence. Passing a few checks—or matching a schema—does not automatically prove a broader kind of conformance.

Conformance is a relation among an exact subject S, exact contract C, declared scope Q, applicable profile P, current evidence set E, and assessment owner. ConstitutionAcceptance: AcceptedVersion: 1.0.0-candidate.1

A versioned, owner-scoped rulebook for selected kinds of subject. Its requirements apply only after the exact version and scope are adopted and the subject matches its selectors; loading it into context does not adopt it.

When it applies
Use a constitution when a recurring class of future subjects needs the same authoritative constraints, ownership, precedence, examples, and validation expectations. Keep one-off advice, observations, and owner decisions outside it. A discipline may gather evidence and route a constitution proposal, but cannot author or adopt the constitution. A validator may check an adopted rule, but cannot supply the authority that the constitution and owner decision provide.
Record formats
Constitution · v1
A stated exclusion
Admission, activation, publication, release, deployment, and external effects.
Formal definition, source explanation and boundaries

The formal statement governs the meaning. The short introduction above helps you read it; it does not replace its requirements.

Source explanatory wording

A constitution is a named rulebook for named things. It says which rules apply, to what, under whose authority, and how conflicts and checks work. It is not a universal prompt for every person, agent, repository, or external system.

Exact governing statement

Constitution is the normalized definition identified by semantic.constitution, owned within scope.shared-authority, and carried by type.definition. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D58 without silently merging it with another target.

Bound source-semantic basis:

A constitution is an **owner-scoped, selector-bound, composable authority artifact** that turns axioms and invariants into reusable governance rules and policies for named kinds of governed subject. Those subjects may be artifacts, tasks or workflows, repository-owned agent actions, system operations or state transitions, validation surfaces, or authority movements.

A constitution must declare its scope, subject kinds, selectors, owner route, authority level, rules and policies, precedence and composition behavior, validation modes or bindings, downstream effect, challenge route, and retirement or split conditions. It constrains a subject only after an owner decision adopts the exact constitution version and scope and the subject matches its selectors. A candidate, selected, or context-loaded constitution does not govern by those facts alone.

```text
Constitution C =
  (id, version, scope, subject_kinds, selectors, rules, policies,
   precedence, composition, owner_route, authority_level,
   validation_bindings, downstream_effect, challenge_route,
   retirement_or_split_rule)

subject_kinds(C) subset-of
  { artifact, task_or_workflow, repository_owned_agent_action,
    system_operation_or_state_transition, validation_surface,
    authority_movement }

applies(C, subject) <->
  promoted(C) and version_exact_owner_adoption(C) and
  subject in scope(C) and selector_matches(C, subject)

validation_mode(rule) in { deterministic, review, hybrid, none-yet }
candidate(C) or selected(C) or context_loaded(C) =/=> applies(C, subject)
```

Schema handle: `CAV2-D58-SCHEMA` — tracked in
[DEFINITION-SCHEMAS.md](DEFINITION-SCHEMAS.md). Status: tracked (documentary);
no machine validator is activated by this definition.
  • A constitution is **not** an axiom (`CAV2-D53`), invariant (`CAV2-D54`), discipline (`CAV2-D50`), decision, validator, gate (`CAV2-D37`), evidence, or proof. Axiom grounds; invariant states what must remain true; governance rule or policy operationalizes; discipline stewards a recurring practice; owner decision adopts; constitution carries the adopted constraints; validator or gate checks or performs enforcement. Authority (`CAV2-D34`) scopes every part of that graph. Promoting this term creates Definition authority for the meaning of `constitution`. It does not promote any constitution artifact, adopt a rule or policy, activate a validation binding, or authorize an effect.

Constraint-Cycle Safety InvariantAcceptance: AcceptedVersion: 1.0.0-candidate.1

Forbids a connection from both constraining another subject’s values and participating in a cycle without an explicit acyclicity constraint. Proposals needing both properties must stop for schema governance and contextuality-obstruction review before influencing work.

When it applies
Use this guard when adding or revising ontology relations, relationship families, edge catalogs, movement edges, schema links, authority transitions, or validation-affecting graph rules. If the new edge can force a value or state and can also form cycles, block the promotion until the review names what constraints could fail to glue, what validator or reviewer will catch that failure, and which owner accepts the remaining residue.
Record formats
No record-type contract in this selected catalog declares this exact definition among the meanings it uses.
A stated exclusion
Admission, activation, publication, release, deployment, and external effects.
Formal definition, source explanation and boundaries

The formal statement governs the meaning. The short introduction above helps you read it; it does not replace its requirements.

Source explanatory wording

An edge can either force a value or freely loop around the graph. If it does both, stop and prove the loop is safe before it becomes a rule.

Exact governing statement

Constraint-Cycle Safety Invariant is the normalized invariant identified by semantic.constraint-cycle-safety-invariant, owned within scope.shared-authority, and carried by type.invariant. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D28 without silently merging it with another target.

Bound source-semantic basis:

A value-cycle edge guard is the CyberAlchemy v2 invariant that no relation, edge type, or ontology movement may simultaneously:

- constrain the value, label, authority state, schema field, or validation outcome of another artifact; and - be allowed to participate in a cycle without an explicit acyclicity constraint.

If a proposed relation needs both properties, it must stop at schema governance and receive a contextuality-obstruction review before it can influence authority, ontology, validation, or implementation.

For any proposed edge type `E`, define two review predicates:

```text
value_constraining(E)
cycle_permitted(E)
```

CyberAlchemy v2 requires:

```text
not (value_constraining(E) and cycle_permitted(E))
```

unless a schema owner records an explicit exception with source evidence,
constraint semantics, satisfiability or obstruction review, validator or review
witness, and typed residue.

The current guard is a watch condition, not a theorem. It is satisfied when
value-constraining edges are acyclic and cycle-permitted edges do not constrain
values. It becomes live only when a proposed edge straddles both classes.
  • Value-cycle edge guard is not a contextuality theorem, not a spectral-presheaf checker, not a ban on cyclic non-value relations, and not a ban on acyclic value constraints. It does not promote any live vault edge family. It only says which edge proposals must be stopped for schema governance and obstruction review.

Contestability PolicyAcceptance: AcceptedVersion: 1.0.0-candidate.1

Declares how a governed object’s meaning, state or claims may be challenged and who handles the response.

When it applies
Use challenge contract when a candidate ontology node, projection, definition proposal, constitution proposal, research claim, or authority artifact needs to say what kind of objection is valid and what happens next. A contradiction edge may block promotion; a validation edge may increase evidence support; a blocking question may defer the node; and unresolved challenge residue must remain attached until an owner route closes, waives, or demotes it.
Record formats
No record-type contract in this selected catalog declares this exact definition among the meanings it uses.
A stated exclusion
Admission, activation, publication, release, deployment, and external effects.
Formal definition, source explanation and boundaries

The formal statement governs the meaning. The short introduction above helps you read it; it does not replace its requirements.

Source explanatory wording

It is the object's "how to disagree with me correctly" field.

Exact governing statement

Contestability Policy is the normalized policy identified by semantic.contestability-policy, owned within scope.shared-authority, and carried by type.policy. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D40 without silently merging it with another target.

Bound source-semantic basis:

A challenge contract is the explicit review surface attached to a CyberAlchemy v2 node, candidate, claim, or authority artifact that states how the object may be challenged, contradicted, validated, blocked, or routed for owner review without silently changing its meaning or confidence.

A challenge contract must declare the valid challenge response, admissible challenge modes, contradiction and validation links when present, owner route, resolution gate, blocking questions, and challenge residue route. It does not contain the object's own confidence or residue and does not introduce a third confidence axis. Object confidence remains a sibling posture using the `evidence_confidence` and `commitment_confidence` split governed by `CAV2-D23`.

An admissible challenge contract has at least:

```text
ChallengeContract =
  (challenge_response, valid_challenge_modes, contradiction_edges,
   validation_edges, owner_route, resolution_gate, blocking_questions,
   challenge_residue_route)
```

where `challenge_residue_route` says where unresolved challenge residue is
handled. The object's own confidence and residue are not part of the challenge
contract. When an object records confidence, active CyberAlchemy v2 uses
`evidence_confidence` for evidence support and `commitment_confidence` for
commitment posture.
  • Challenge contract is not a verdict, not a confidence score, not proof of truth, not a promotion decision, and not an ontology-owned override of the relevant owner route. It names the challenge path; owner routes and gates still decide movement.

ContextAcceptance: AcceptedVersion: 1.0.0-candidate.1

A stable frame of relevance and interpretation for one purpose, anchored to exactly one product and, when applicable, one project and one goal, with explicit consumers and source rules.

When it applies
Create a Context before assembling a reusable context view for a Product, Project, or Goal. Keep the Context identity and purpose stable, then let a resolver create immutable Views bound to exact requests and source epochs. Consumers may reuse the Context identity across CLI, chat, and session continuations, but they must not silently reuse a stale View.
Record formats
Context · v1
A stated exclusion
Admission, activation, publication, release, deployment, and external effects.
Formal definition, source explanation and boundaries

The formal statement governs the meaning. The short introduction above helps you read it; it does not replace its requirements.

Source explanatory wording

A context is the stable boundary that says what information and meaning matter for one purpose.

Exact governing statement

Context is the normalized definition identified by semantic.context, owned within scope.context-resolution, and carried by type.definition. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D66 without silently merging it with another target.

Target-specific normative meaning:

A Context is a durable, identity-bearing, owner-qualified boundary of relevance and interpretation for one declared purpose, anchored to exactly one Product and, when applicable, one Project and one Goal, with explicit consumers, subject scope, and source policies.

Bound source-semantic basis:

A Context is a durable, identity-bearing, owner-qualified boundary of relevance and interpretation for one declared purpose. It names the Product, optional Project, optional Goal, intended consumers and uses, subject scope, and source policies that frame what information and meaning may be assembled for the work.

Every CyberAlchemy Context belongs to exactly one Product. A project Context belongs to exactly one Project. A goal Context belongs to exactly one Project and focuses on exactly one Goal that already belongs to that Project. The first contract intentionally allows only one primary Goal per Context; cross-goal work requires separate Contexts or a later explicitly defined composite model.

A Context identity remains stable across new source epochs, resolution requests, immutable views, interface presentations, session pauses, and refreshes that preserve its Product, Project, Goal, and purpose. A material change to any of those anchors creates a successor Context and supersedes the earlier one instead of silently changing what the earlier identity meant.

Exact governing statement

A Context Map is a versioned, owner-approved set of exact Bounded Context endpoints and typed directional relationships between them. The Context Map is the sole canonical owner of its endpoint membership and relationships.   • Direction and authority limits cannot be inferred from imports.
  • One mapping pattern is selected by its owners, not by this generic definition.

Source explanatory wording

Exact governing statement

Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D66 without silently merging it with another target.

Target-specific normative meaning:

A Context Request is a bounded, attributable request to resolve a declared Context for named consumers and intended uses under exact selectors, freshness requirements, exclusions, and output constraints; it neither mutates the Context nor grants authority over selected sources.

Bound source-semantic basis:

A Context is a durable, identity-bearing, owner-qualified boundary of relevance and interpretation for one declared purpose. It names the Product, optional Project, optional Goal, intended consumers and uses, subject scope, and source policies that frame what information and meaning may be assembled for the work.

Every CyberAlchemy Context belongs to exactly one Product. A project Context belongs to exactly one Project. A goal Context belongs to exactly one Project and focuses on exactly one Goal that already belongs to that Project. The first contract intentionally allows only one primary Goal per Context; cross-goal work requires separate Contexts or a later explicitly defined composite model.

A Context identity remains stable across new source epochs, resolution requests, immutable views, interface presentations, session pauses, and refreshes that preserve its Product, Project, Goal, and purpose. A material change to any of those anchors creates a successor Context and supersedes the earlier one instead of silently changing what the earlier identity meant.

CyberAlchemy Construction MethodAcceptance: AcceptedVersion: 1.0.0-candidate.1

The governed construction path from a product intent to an implementation that can be reviewed, assessed, operated and changed.

When it applies
Use Craft method whenever CyberAlchemy builds or materially evolves a Product, Product Feature, Product Capability, system, or implementation-bearing capability. Begin from the Product and Project context, define the meaning, model the product and business obligations, author or update the DomainSpec source, select exact realizations, construct the target, independently check it, observe bounded runtime behavior, preserve recovery and evolution obligations, and route the evidenced state to its owner.
Record formats
No record-type contract in this selected catalog declares this exact definition among the meanings it uses.
A stated exclusion
Admission, activation, publication, release, deployment, and external effects.
Formal definition, source explanation and boundaries

The formal statement governs the meaning. The short introduction above helps you read it; it does not replace its requirements.

Source explanatory wording

It is the whole governed path for turning product intent into a working, reviewable system.

Exact governing statement

CyberAlchemy Construction Method is the normalized method identified by semantic.cyberalchemy-construction-method, owned within scope.construction, and carried by type.method. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D20 without silently merging it with another target.

Target-specific normative meaning:

CyberAlchemy Construction Method is the governed recursive method that carries owner-controlled Product intent through explicit context, semantic, product, specification, realization, conformance, operation, recovery, evolution, and continuation stages while preserving evidence and residue at every transition.

Bound source-semantic basis:

Craft method is CyberAlchemy's governed recursive system-building method. It turns owner-controlled Product intent into an evidence-bounded working system by preserving one explicit chain through context, definitions, product and business meaning, system specification, exact realization selection, deterministic construction, independent conformance, bounded operation, recovery, evolution, and owner continuation.

The method uses a source-of-truth ledger to preserve state across that chain. It records contexts, candidate definitions, blockers, enablers, decisions, gaps, artifacts, next moves, validation evidence, residue, and recomposition obligations. Ledgering is the method's continuity mechanism; it is not the whole method.

In CyberAlchemy v2, Craft method is valid only when it preserves these boundaries:

- a Product and its Product Thesis own product purpose and value propositions - a Project coordinates the goals, owners, evidence, decisions, and work used to develop or evolve the Product - Product Features and Product Capabilities remain distinct from the Product, Project, Method, and their realizations - canonical definitions, product and business ontology, DomainSpec source, generated system ontology, realization selection, construction, conformance, runtime evidence, and owner decisions remain separately identifiable - every implementation-bearing construction follows the exact `CAV2-D65` DomainSpec-governed construction chain or carries typed residue for the missing prerequisite - `Craft ledger` or an equivalent declared ledger is the source of truth for Craft state - `CRAFT.md`, `Craft index`, projections, and status output are derived views - residue is typed and carried forward instead of hidden - schema-level and instance-level validation are not collapsed - child contexts recompose into their parent through evidence - closure happens by owner decision, gate, or accepted residue, not by a claim of total final completion - Craft state can carry local candidate definitions and receipts but cannot make terms canonical without definitions-governance

For a bounded Product and Project scope `S`, the Craft method has the minimum
governed shape:

```text
M_Craft(S) =
  (context, product_intent, domain_meaning, system_specification,
   realization_selection, construction, conformance, operation,
   recovery_and_evolution, owner_continuation, ledger_state)

L_S = (C, B, E, D, G, A, N, R)
```

where:

- `context` resolves the Product, Project, Goal, participants, consumers, and
  source policies relevant to the bounded work
- `product_intent` carries the Product Thesis plus selected Product Feature or
  Product Capability obligations
- `domain_meaning` carries canonical definitions and product/business ontology
- `system_specification` carries DomainSpec and generated system-ontology state
- `realization_selection` identifies exact architecture and language-profile
  realizations
- `construction` materializes the selected contained target deterministically
- `conformance` independently evaluates declared static and relational
  obligations
- `operation` supplies bounded runtime evidence without becoming authority
- `recovery_and_evolution` preserves compensation, recovery, migration,
  rollback, compatibility, and successor-state obligations
- `owner_continuation` routes an evidenced next state to its explicit owner
- `C` is the set of contexts or child contexts
- `B` is blockers
- `E` is enablers or available evidence
- `D` is decisions
- `G` is gaps or unresolved obligations
- `A` is artifacts and source references
- `N` is next moves or route obligations
- `R` is typed residue plus recomposition evidence

A Craft step is admissible when it preserves typed identity and source
authority, records the operation that changed state, keeps generated views
derivative, validates every reachable declared consumer, and either repairs,
types, routes, accepts, or defers residue with an owner. Construction does not
establish conformance; conformance does not establish runtime truth; evidence
does not establish owner adoption or permission.

Formal-foundations evidence supports this shape by treating residue as typed and
composable, by separating schema-fidelity from instance-fidelity, by showing
that reflection towers assemble without finite total closure, and by justifying
stop criteria based on decision and residue plateau rather than completion. This
is support evidence for the method; it does not prove that an LLM-centered Craft
run achieved a clean functor, kernel, or zero-residue translation.
  • Craft method is not the Craft Product, Craft Project, a Product Feature, Product Capability, Product Thesis, DomainSpec model, architecture pattern, generator, runtime, public Arcanum capability, `.craft` state, generic task runner, or replacement for task-session. It is not a source of canonical definitions and does not authorize implementation or prove that a translation, construction, conformance assessment, operation, recovery, or migration is complete. It may use formal foundations as support evidence, but it must preserve their honesty boundary: formal cousins describe the structure Craft operates inside; they do not certify that a particular Craft run achieved the clean formal case. Craft method also does not promote `ledger` as a cross-method primitive by itself. Ledger remains separately flagged for review until recursivity, relation inheritance, and local Craft ledger conformance are settled.
  • This target remains distinct from the sibling targets semantic.residue-escalation-method, semantic.work-state-continuity-capability reconstructed from CAV2-D20; shared source lineage does not merge their identities or validation purposes.

Formal definition, source explanation and boundaries

The formal statement governs the meaning. The short introduction above helps you read it; it does not replace its requirements.

Source explanatory wording

Several exact decisions shown together once. The person sees one interaction, but each decision keeps its own owner, target, and consequence.

Exact governing statement

A Decision Bundle is a closed ordered set of exact Governance Decision requests presented at one Decision Checkpoint. Every member retains an independent decision identity, Authority Boundary, owner role, accountable principal, immutable target, digest when bytes exist, requested effect, scope, outcome, and invalidation conditions. Bundling reduces human interaction count but cannot merge roles, infer authorization between members, or make one member's outcome satisfy another member's gate.

DecisionBundle(B,c) iff FiniteClosed(B) and forall d in B: Checkpoint(d)=c and ExactTarget(d) and ExactOwner(d) and ExactEffect(d). Authority(B) = union of no implicit authority; Authorized(B) iff forall d in B: Authorized(d).
  • A shared principal does not collapse member owner roles.
  • One approved member does not approve another member.
  • A member whose exact target does not yet exist cannot enter the bundle.

  • Approval is one possible decision outcome, not the checkpoint itself.
  • Grouping decisions at one checkpoint does not merge their Authority Boundaries.
  • A checkpoint cannot bind unknown future bytes when the required decision targets exact output bytes.

DefinitionAcceptance: AcceptedVersion: 1.0.0-candidate.1

An owner-controlled record stating exactly what a term means, where that meaning applies and how drift can be challenged. Acceptance is separate from draft checks or explanatory wording.

When it applies
When a shared meaning needs an exact version, accountable owner, scope and boundaries.
Record formats
Definition · v2
In the Northstar incident
The owner-accepted completeness criterion governs identifier coverage for Northstar, the declared filters and S1.
Common mistake
Treating a generated summary or an unaccepted draft as an accepted definition.
Formal definition, source explanation and boundaries

The formal statement governs the meaning. The short introduction above helps you read it; it does not replace its requirements.

Source explanatory wording

The project-owned record that says exactly what a term means, where that meaning applies, and how drift can be challenged. A passing candidate is not canonical until its owner admits it.

Exact governing statement

A Definition is a versioned, owner-scoped semantic artifact that assigns a term one normative meaning within an exact authority scope. It is structurally complete only when stable identity, applicability, exclusions, a scientific/formal normative voice, explicitly non-normative plain-language and domain-context voices, boundaries, admitted source posture, primary consumers, a synchronized registry postimage, generated index, and a current drift route are declared. Only an exact owner promotion decision can make one exact Definition version canonical authority.

Exact Publication Authorization InvariantAcceptance: AcceptedVersion: 1.0.0-candidate.1

For private material, each source owner must authorize an exact candidate slice and its permitted use. After private generation and validation, the publishing principal separately approves the exact finished bytes, audience, channel and claim limits.

When it applies
Use this definition when someone wants to turn private DomainSpec, CAV2, proof-substrate, Mint, Cedar, Datalog, Lean, research, evidence, or generated material into a public-safe output. First ask each source owner exactly what may be used and said. Generate and check the candidate privately. Then ask the named publishing principal about the final bytes, not a template or promise. If any bound input or output changes, return to the relevant decision.
Record formats
No record-type contract in this selected catalog declares this exact definition among the meanings it uses.
A stated exclusion
Admission, activation, publication, release, deployment, and external effects.
Formal definition, source explanation and boundaries

The formal statement governs the meaning. The short introduction above helps you read it; it does not replace its requirements.

Source explanatory wording

Permission to prepare a public draft is not permission to publish it. Owners first approve the ingredients and limits; a publisher later approves the exact finished file and destination.

Exact governing statement

Exact Publication Authorization Invariant is the normalized invariant identified by semantic.exact-publication-authorization-invariant, owned within scope.repository-governance, and carried by type.invariant. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D57 without silently merging it with another target.

Bound source-semantic basis:

Exact publication authorization is the CyberAlchemy v2 rule that private material may cross a publication boundary only after two separate decisions:

1. every source owner authorizes an exact candidate slice, its allowed claims, audience, channel, privacy policies, and requested publishing principal; and 2. after private generation and privacy validation, that publishing principal approves the exact final output bytes, digest, audience, channel, and claim ceiling.

The first decision permits creation and review of a private publication candidate. It does not permit unknown future bytes to be published. The second decision applies only to the exact output it binds. Any change to the sources, claims, policies, generator, output bytes, audience, channel, or publishing principal requires the applicable decisions to be repeated.

All material is private by default when no valid exact authorization exists. Generation, validation, proof, obligation discharge, CAV2 promotion, or domain adoption does not grant publication permission.

```text
PublicationAuthorization =
  (release_authorizations, exact_output_approval, publication_receipt?)

publishable(output, audience, channel)
  <-> every contributing source has a valid exact release authorization
      and privacy_validation(output) = pass
      and exact_output_approval binds
          (output bytes, output digest, audience, channel, claim ceiling)

generated(output) =/=> publishable(output, audience, channel)
validated(output) =/=> publishable(output, audience, channel)
promoted(output)  =/=> publishable(output, audience, channel)
```

Source owners and the publishing principal are separate authority roles. A
generator or validator may check that bindings exist and match; it cannot act as
either owner unless a separate authority decision explicitly assigns that role.
  • Exact publication authorization is not classification authority, adoption, promotion, proof, truth, freshness, privacy validation, deployment, or release by itself. It does not create a universal classification vocabulary: each source owner retains its own meanings, and a projection carries exact owner-qualified references without reinterpreting them. It authorizes no present public output; every actual publication still needs exact permissions and a boundary-crossing receipt.

A route for turning interface observations and lessons into proposed reusable rules through evidence, later use, challenge and owner review.

When it applies
Use experience evidence lifecycle when harvesting a UI session, distilling a UX pattern, producing a validator claim map, preparing a studio mutation intent, or deciding whether repeated interface evidence should become a reusable rule.
Record formats
No record-type contract in this selected catalog declares this exact definition among the meanings it uses.
A stated exclusion
Admission, activation, publication, release, deployment, and external effects.
Formal definition, source explanation and boundaries

The formal statement governs the meaning. The short introduction above helps you read it; it does not replace its requirements.

Source explanatory wording

A UI lesson becomes a rule only after it earns its way through evidence, repeat-use, challenge, and owner review.

Exact governing statement

Experience Evidence Formation Method is the normalized method identified by semantic.experience-evidence-formation-method, owned within scope.ux-ui, and carried by type.method. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D46 without silently merging it with another target.

Bound source-semantic basis:

Experience evidence lifecycle is the CyberAlchemy v2 lifecycle by which an interface observation or UI iteration becomes reusable UX/UI knowledge only after evidence capture, lesson formation, pattern distillation, validator or studio handoff, cross-session exercise, challenge, and owner promotion.

The normal path is:

```text interface observation or UI hypothesis -> browser/user/session evidence -> lesson -> ux-pattern candidate -> validator claim map or studio annotation intent -> fixture, browser, or cross-session exercise -> challenge and residue review -> owner promotion -> UX/UI pattern, validator rule, or interface constraint authority ```

An interface pattern is not authoritative because it looked better once. It must carry evidence and survive the claim class appropriate to its evidence.

For experience candidate `e`, the lifecycle is:

```text
EEL(e) =
  (observation, evidence, lesson, pattern_candidate,
   consumer_handoff, exercise, challenge, owner_decision,
   authority_effect, residue)
```

Movement to authority is admissible only when the owner decision names the
authority effect and the claim class is valid for the supporting evidence.
  • Experience evidence lifecycle is not a usability study by itself, not a browser test result by itself, not a studio approval path, and not a guarantee that a subjective UX claim can become deterministic.

Experiment DesignAcceptance: AcceptedVersion: 1.0.0-candidate.1

The plan specifying conditions, variables, measurements, comparisons and stopping rules before an experiment is claimed to have run.

When it applies
Use an Experiment when a Project needs observations created by a repeatable test rather than only existing sources or argument. Freeze the protocol inputs and claim limits before treating run output as comparable evidence. Keep design, run evidence, analysis, and owner decisions distinct.
Record formats
Experiment design · v1
A stated exclusion
Admission, activation, publication, release, deployment, and external effects.
Formal definition, source explanation and boundaries

The formal statement governs the meaning. The short introduction above helps you read it; it does not replace its requirements.

Source explanatory wording

It is the test plan written before anyone claims the test was performed.

Exact governing statement

Experiment Design is the normalized definition identified by semantic.experiment-design, owned within scope.knowledge-development, and carried by type.definition. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D62 without silently merging it with another target.

Target-specific normative meaning:

An Experiment Design is the pre-run specification of a bounded empirical test, including its question or hypothesis, subject, protocol, conditions, variables or interventions, measures, prerequisites, stop rules, owner route, and challenge route.

Bound source-semantic basis:

An experiment is a bounded, attributable empirical test that produces observations by applying a declared protocol to a defined subject under named conditions in order to test a question, hypothesis, Goal condition, or Research question.

An Experiment artifact must preserve its Project and Goal links, Research links when present, question or hypothesis, subject, protocol, conditions, variables or interventions, measures, environment, prerequisites, stop rules, run references, evidence references, findings references, limitations, owner route, and challenge route. Missing run evidence means the experiment was not shown to have run.

```text
Experiment =
  (id, project_ref, goal_refs, research_refs, question_or_hypothesis,
   subject, protocol_ref, conditions, variables_or_interventions,
   measures, environment, prerequisites, stop_rules, run_refs,
   evidence_refs, findings_refs, limitations, created, last_updated,
   owner_route, challenge_route)

ran(Experiment) only if valid_run_refs_exist
concluded(Experiment) only through separate Findings or owner decision
```
  • An experiment is not Research (`CAV2-D61`), a Goal (`CAV2-D59`), a plan, a runtime, a test suite, one command, findings, causal proof, or authority to run. It is an ephemeral canonical Evidence artifact. A successful validator can show that its record is well formed; it cannot show that the experiment ran or that its hypothesis is true.
  • This target remains distinct from the sibling targets semantic.experiment-run, semantic.observation reconstructed from CAV2-D62; shared source lineage does not merge their identities or validation purposes.

FindingAcceptance: AcceptedVersion: 1.0.0-candidate.1

An attributable conclusion stating what the evidence supports and its limits. It is not automatically a decision or policy.

When it applies
Use Research when a Project must inspect literature, repositories, benchmarks, past evidence, observations, or competing explanations before deciding what to believe or do. Keep the aggregate separate from findings so a later reader can see the source material without inheriting the synthesis as fact.
Record formats
Finding · v1
A stated exclusion
Admission, activation, publication, release, deployment, and external effects.
Formal definition, source explanation and boundaries

The formal statement governs the meaning. The short introduction above helps you read it; it does not replace its requirements.

Source explanatory wording

A finding is what the evidence currently supports saying; it is not automatically a decision or policy.

Exact governing statement

Finding is the normalized definition identified by semantic.finding, owned within scope.knowledge-development, and carried by type.definition. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D61 without silently merging it with another target.

Target-specific normative meaning:

A Finding is an evidence-bounded, attributable conclusion derived from one or more Research Runs or Evidence Sets whose claim wording does not exceed its support and whose limitations and challenge route remain explicit.

Bound source-semantic basis:

Research is a bounded, attributable investigation that gathers and organizes source material and observations to answer one declared question for a Project and one or more Goals.

A Research artifact must preserve its question, scope, sources, method, evidence aggregate, counterevidence, limitations, owner route, Goal and Project links, and references to any separate findings. Research records what was investigated and gathered. It does not silently turn its evidence aggregate into a conclusion, decision, definition, specification, or product claim.

```text
Research =
  (id, project_ref, goal_refs, question, scope, sources, method,
   evidence_aggregate, counterevidence, findings_refs, limitations,
   created, last_updated, owner_route, challenge_route)

Research.outcome is absent
Findings.question = Research.question
Findings derives_from Research
```
  • Research is not a Goal (`CAV2-D59`), Project (`CAV2-D60`), experiment (`CAV2-D62`), findings, owner decision, canonical definition, proof, or execution authority. It is an ephemeral canonical Evidence artifact: it records an investigation at a time and cannot become authority by promotion.
  • This target remains distinct from the sibling targets semantic.evidence-set, semantic.research-inquiry, semantic.research-run reconstructed from CAV2-D61; shared source lineage does not merge their identities or validation purposes.

Four-Facet Artifact InvariantAcceptance: AcceptedVersion: 1.0.0-candidate.1

Requires governed actions to identify classification, schema, a human-continuation view and a machine-checkable view. Missing aspects must be recorded with an owner and whether work may continue, wait or is blocked.

When it applies
Use this method before or during any CyberAlchemy v2 action that may matter later: definition work, constitution work, axiom work, discipline work, Craft state changes, ontology projections, task execution, workflow design, system design, validation, or implementation routing.
Record formats
No record-type contract in this selected catalog declares this exact definition among the meanings it uses.
A stated exclusion
Admission, activation, publication, release, deployment, and external effects.
Formal definition, source explanation and boundaries

The formal statement governs the meaning. The short introduction above helps you read it; it does not replace its requirements.

Source explanatory wording

Before an action is allowed to matter, it must answer four questions: what kind of thing is this, what shape governs it, how can a human continue it, and how can a machine check it? If one answer is missing, write down the missing piece, who owns it, and whether the action can continue.

Exact governing statement

Four-Facet Artifact Invariant is the normalized invariant identified by semantic.four-facet-artifact-invariant, owned within scope.shared-authority, and carried by type.invariant. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D21 without silently merging it with another target.

Bound source-semantic basis:

Four-facet action method is the CyberAlchemy v2 primitive action rule that every governed action must explicitly bind, create, or record typed residue for four facets before the action can govern downstream work:

- classification or taxonomy facet - schema facet - human-continuation view - machine-checkable view

A governed action is any CyberAlchemy v2 action that creates, changes, routes, validates, promotes, implements, or interprets load-bearing artifacts, state, meaning, or authority posture. The action is admissible only when each facet is declared or when its absence is carried as typed residue.

At minimum:

- the classification or taxonomy facet states what kind of thing or action is involved and which classification catalog, taxonomy, or source vocabulary owns that assignment - the schema facet states the structural shape, field set, relation shape, or validation surface that governs the action or artifact - the human-continuation view states how a human can understand the action's purpose, status, trust boundary, blockers, residue, next route, and evidence - the machine-checkable view states how a machine can parse or check the action state, including identifiers, kind, schema reference, classification reference, source of truth, validator or proof handle, projection status, and residue

If a facet is missing, impossible, or intentionally deferred, the action must record typed residue naming the missing facet, the reason or impossibility, the owner route, the evidence reference, and the action effect: continue, defer, or block. If the action later asks to promote something, the same residue must also state the promotion effect.

For a governed action `a`, let:

```text
F(a) = (K_a, S_a, H_a, M_a, R_a)
```

where:

- `K_a` is the classification or taxonomy facet
- `S_a` is the schema facet
- `H_a` is the human-continuation view
- `M_a` is the machine-checkable view
- `R_a` is typed residue for any missing, impossible, or deferred facet

The action satisfies the four-facet action method when each of `K_a`, `S_a`,
`H_a`, and `M_a` is either bound to an existing governed surface, created by the
action, or represented in `R_a` with owner route and effect. The method forbids
silent absence; it does not require perfect completion before exploratory work
can begin.
  • Four-facet action method is not a promotion gate by itself, not proof of authority, not a requirement that all exploratory work have perfect schemas before it starts, and not a single required file format. It allows an action to create missing facets or carry typed residue. Generic `schema` semantics are defined locally by `CAV2-D56`; `DEF-ARC-SCHEMA` remains Arcanum's public surface and this definition's non-normative ancestor. A classification facet is not ontology membership or promotion. A human-continuation view is not canonical merely because it is readable. A machine-checkable view is not authority and is not proof beyond the named checks it can actually run.

GateAcceptance: AcceptedVersion: 1.0.0-candidate.1

An owner-scoped checkpoint deciding or routing whether a candidate may proceed, proceed with named risk, stop or defer. Its criteria, evidence, verdicts and consequences must be explicit.

When it applies
Use a promotion gate whenever a claim would cross from source evidence, inventory, ontology, research, observability, or memory into definitions, constitutions, specs, capabilities, implementation, or public-facing material.
Record formats
No record-type contract in this selected catalog declares this exact definition among the meanings it uses.
A stated exclusion
Admission, activation, publication, release, deployment, and external effects.
Formal definition, source explanation and boundaries

The formal statement governs the meaning. The short introduction above helps you read it; it does not replace its requirements.

Source explanatory wording

A promotion gate is the moment the project asks, "is this allowed to count now?" A gate is the checkpoint that says "go", "go with this named risk", "stop", or "send this to the right owner first."

Exact governing statement

Gate is the normalized definition identified by semantic.gate, owned within scope.shared-authority, and carried by type.definition. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D5, CAV2-D37 without silently merging it with another target.

Bound source-semantic basis:

A promotion gate is an explicit owner route that decides whether evidence, candidate meaning, a recurring practice, or a structural rule may become local authority, implementation work, or standalone repository material.

A gate is an explicit checkpoint that decides or routes whether a candidate term, rule, artifact, relation, method, claim, mutation, or execution may continue, must continue with named risk, must stop, or must defer to another owner.

Every CyberAlchemy v2 gate must declare its owner route, scope, inputs, criteria, possible verdicts, required evidence, residue handling, record location, and downstream effect. Unless a narrower gate defines otherwise, the minimum verdict vocabulary is `pass`, `flag`, `block`, and `defer`.

A gate `G` is a decision function:

```text
G(scope, input, evidence, criteria) -> verdict
verdict in {pass, flag, block, defer}
```

The verdict is admissible only if it records owner route, evidence basis,
residue or risk when present, and downstream effect.
  • The gate may return pass, flag, or block. A flag is not a silent pass; it carries named risk and follow-up.
  • Gate is not bureaucracy, not a checklist item by itself, not permission without a record, and not proof of correctness. A gate may use validators or human decisions, but the gate is the recorded transition logic and effect.

Govern UX/UI KnowledgeAcceptance: AcceptedVersion: 1.0.0-candidate.1

The process for retaining and reviewing interface evidence and lessons without treating appearance, screenshots or passing browser checks as proof of human experience.

When it applies
Use UX/UI knowledge governance when UI work produces reusable lessons, design patterns, validation claims, accessibility claims, layout evidence, interaction evidence, or subjective experience claims. Route lesson capture through `ux-lessons`, validator-safe evidence through `ux-evidence-validator`, studio mutation intents through `ui-prototyping-studio`, and promotion through the CyberAlchemy authority model.
Record formats
No record-type contract in this selected catalog declares this exact definition among the meanings it uses.
A stated exclusion
Admission, activation, publication, release, deployment, and external effects.
Formal definition, source explanation and boundaries

The formal statement governs the meaning. The short introduction above helps you read it; it does not replace its requirements.

Source explanatory wording

UX/UI governance is how the project remembers interface learning without pretending that a nice-looking screen, a screenshot, or a passing browser test is automatically truth.

Exact governing statement

Govern UX/UI Knowledge is the normalized product-capability identified by semantic.govern-ux-ui-knowledge-capability, owned within scope.ux-ui, and carried by type.product-capability. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D45 without silently merging it with another target.

Bound source-semantic basis:

UX/UI knowledge governance is the CyberAlchemy v2 lens-specific governance interface that turns interface iteration, browser evidence, accessibility evidence, visual evidence, interaction traces, user-study residue, and reusable experience lessons into governed candidates without treating subjective experience quality as automatic authority.

It must separate at least these lanes:

- captured interface lesson - reusable UX/UI pattern candidate - browser-observable evidence - accessibility and semantic evidence - layout and interaction evidence - cognitive or attention risk proxy - domain-practice heuristic - human-study or expert-review residue - promotion request and owner decision

UX/UI knowledge governance can produce candidate lessons, patterns, claim maps, validator specs, fixture plans, studio annotation intents, evidence reports, and promotion requests. It does not promote UX/UI authority by itself.

For interface knowledge object `u`, CyberAlchemy v2 tracks:

```text
UXG(u) =
  (lesson_ref, pattern_candidate, browser_evidence, accessibility_evidence,
   layout_interaction_evidence, cognitive_attention_proxy,
   domain_practice_claim, human_study_residue,
   owner_route, promotion_path, challenge_contract)
```

The object is authority-bearing only when the relevant owner route records the
promotion effect and the claim strength remains bounded by available evidence.
  • UX/UI knowledge governance is not a universal UX score, not an accessibility certificate, not a design-system authority, not a human-study substitute, not a studio mutation approval, and not a promotion event.

Governance-Axis Independence InvariantAcceptance: AcceptedVersion: 1.0.0-candidate.1

Requires kind, status, evidence confidence, commitment confidence, provenance and owner to remain distinct when they matter to a decision. One dimension cannot silently answer another: acceptance does not establish strong evidence.

When it applies
Use authority lifecycle axes when evaluating definitions, constitutions, axioms, ontology nodes, inventory cards, task results, schemas, and implementation claims. The reviewer should ask which axis is being advanced: source role, maturity, evidence, owner commitment, provenance, or canonical authority.
Record formats
No record-type contract in this selected catalog declares this exact definition among the meanings it uses.
A stated exclusion
Admission, activation, publication, release, deployment, and external effects.
Formal definition, source explanation and boundaries

The formal statement governs the meaning. The short introduction above helps you read it; it does not replace its requirements.

Source explanatory wording

"Useful", "trusted", "finished", "owned", and "canonical" are different words. Do not let one of them impersonate the others.

Exact governing statement

Governance-Axis Independence Invariant is the normalized invariant identified by semantic.governance-axis-independence-invariant, owned within scope.shared-authority, and carried by type.invariant. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D23 without silently merging it with another target.

Bound source-semantic basis:

Authority lifecycle axis is the CyberAlchemy v2 rule that authority posture must separate at least these dimensions when they matter to a decision:

- role or kind - maturity or status - evidence confidence - commitment or conviction - provenance - owner

No one axis may silently stand in for another. A definition can be mature but weakly evidenced, an imported source can be well-evidenced but not locally canonical, an ontology candidate can be useful but unpromoted, and an owner can be committed to a hypothesis without that hypothesis becoming authority.

An authority-bearing artifact `a` has lifecycle posture:

```text
L(a) = (kind, status, evidence, commitment, provenance, owner, residue)
```

where each component may be known, unknown, deferred, or source-local. A
governance move is valid only if it changes the intended component and does not
imply changes to the others unless those changes are explicitly recorded.
  • Authority lifecycle axis is not a complete status schema and does not make every artifact an ontology node. It gives the minimum separations that future schemas, ledgers, and constitutions must preserve.
